full_judgment:
Abu Sayeed Ahammed J: This Rule was issued on 14-8-94 at the instance of Mirza Anwarul Islam alias Tanu, the accused petitioner for quashing the proceedings of case No. 275C/92, pending before the court of District Magistrate, Dinajpur Sadar, Dinajpur under section 7 A of Telegraph Act, 1885. 

 2. Facts in this case, in short, is that, the Accounts Officer, Telephone (Revenue), Rangpur filed a petition of complaint on 20-7-1992 leading to complaint case TR/Court Case/Special/Dinajpur 4388/92-93 for realisation of a sum of Taka 96,608/85 being the arrear telephone bill, on the allegation that though repeated demands. for the same was made but the defaulter accused petitioner has not paid the bill and, as .such, the Telephone Authority came up with the application under section 7A of Telephone Act, 1885 alleging that because of default the arrear bill has usurped the character of fine and it is realisable under section 396(1) (a) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 3, Section 7A of the Telegraph Act, 1885 reads as follows: 

 So, it is very distinct and clear that the realising authority may take step for realisation of the arrear dues for telephone use, under section 7(a), (as amended) of the Telegraph Act, 1885. The learned Additional Attorney General took interest in the conflict and he has enlightened us with the latest amendment as made in section 7 of the Telegraph Act, 1885. So, the learned Counsel for the defaulter petitioner Md Bazlul Gani although argues that the arrear bills can be realised through the procedure as adopted in PDR Act it cannot be accepted. It is an option of the realising authority. It can also take shelter of section 7(a) of the Telegraph Act. Arrear bill for the telephonic message is not denied by the learned Counsel of the petitioner. So, the arrear dues of the telephone bill can be legally realised under section 7(a) of the said Act, giving up going to the PDR Act.
